If a deposit is blended with others, we say so honestly rather than pretend an exact split. This is the groundwork; the 'by recommendation' view in your Outcomes page lands next.

entries.title: New updates now always appear at the top
entries.body: We fixed the ordering of this Updates feed: when several updates share the same day, the newest one now always shows at the very top instead of occasionally slotting in among the others. A small thing, but it means the entry at the top is always the latest.

entries.title: Review and sign AI-suggested vault moves — right in chat
entries.body: You can now act on an AI-suggested vault move in one place, right in the chat. When you tap 'Review this move' on a suggestion, we build a single safety-checked transaction — run through our deterministic policy engine and a real on-chain dry-run — show you every guardrail and every balance change, and let you sign it from your own wallet. The recipient is always your own wallet, SparkPoint never holds your keys or signs for you, and withdrawals are never blocked by a check, a pause, or a fee. Nothing moves until you sign.

entries.title: Your real wallet in onboarding, and clearer example labels
entries.body: Onboarding now shows your actual connected wallet address instead of a placeholder, and any example figures in the walkthrough are clearly marked as examples — while your real numbers (APY, balances) are read live on-chain. Part of our 'provable, not promised' commitment: we would rather show nothing than a number that is not real.

entries.title: Your Outcome Log now shows real results
entries.body: The Outcome Log now lists your real realized results — one row per withdrawal, wins and losses alike, each linking to its on-chain transaction as proof. Every figure is computed from your own deposits and withdrawals; when your on-chain history can't be fully reconciled we show an honest empty state instead of a guess. These are position-level results — not yet tied to the specific recommendation that caused them.

entries.title: We now dry-run your deposit before you sign
entries.body: Before you sign a vault deposit, we run a real on-chain dry-run of the exact transaction — so if it would fail, we tell you why and disable signing instead of letting you waste gas on a doomed transaction. Withdrawals are untouched: the dry-run there is advisory only and never blocks your exit. And if you still need to approve USDC first, we say so plainly rather than showing a scary error.

entries.title: Your portfolio now shows realized profit — correctly
entries.body: Your portfolio and position detail now show a real realized-PnL figure (profit you booked on past withdrawals) plus a corrected unrealized figure, both derived from your on-chain deposits and withdrawals. Cost basis is now the average cost of the shares you still hold. When the on-chain history can't be fully reconciled, we show 'pending' rather than a guess.

entries.title: APY now reads the live on-chain Aave rate
entries.body: The vault, the deposit confirmation, and recommendation cards now show the net APY computed from the live Aave supply rate read on-chain — no more placeholder number. On the current testnet, where the rate is effectively zero, it honestly shows '≈0% (testnet)', and '—' if the rate can't be read.

entries.title: A more honest fees page
entries.body: The Fees page no longer shows an illustrative revenue chart or a placeholder 'fees paid' number. It now states the live, on-chain performance-fee terms and explains plainly that we don't show a per-wallet fees-paid figure because the fee is share dilution to a shared recipient — we'd rather show nothing than a fabricated number.

entries.title: See exactly which protocols the AI can touch
entries.body: The Trust Center now lists the closed set of on-chain venues Sparky is allowed to route into — on this network, just Aave v3 — each with its real contract address and a block-explorer link. The AI can call nothing outside this audited allowlist, and it's read straight from the on-chain policy.

entries.title: Your settings now stick
entries.body: Notification toggles and display preferences are saved on your device, so they survive a reload — and Compact density and Reduce-motion now actually apply across the app. (Notification delivery itself isn't live yet; the toggles record what you'll get once it is.)

entries.title: Fixed a false “switch network” message when signing in
entries.body: If your wallet was already on Base Sepolia or Robinhood Testnet, the sign-in screen could still say “wrong network” while your wallet was reconnecting — with no way forward. It now waits for your wallet to settle before deciding, adds in-app “Switch to Base Sepolia” and “Use Robinhood Testnet” buttons so you can fix it in one click, and no longer sends you back to the connect screen mid-reconnect.

entries.title: Your plan is now saved exactly as you set it
entries.body: When you finish onboarding, Sparky now saves the exact goal, risk level, and time horizon you chose — before, it could quietly fall back to a default. You'll also see your real plan in Settings, the chat sidebar, and your portfolio, with a clear Saving/❯ retry state when you confirm.

entries.title: Recommendations now show their reasoning and sources
entries.body: Every strategy suggestion now explains itself in plain language under “Why this?” and shows the sources it drew on, so you can see the thinking behind a move — not just the number.

entries.title: Clearer fee terms before you deposit
entries.body: The deposit screen now spells out our fee in full every time you sign — 10% of yield only, above a high-water mark, 0% on your principal and 0% management fee — and your withdrawal receipt restates it. We only earn when you earn.

entries.title: Deposit caps now read live from the chain
entries.body: The per-user, total, and vault deposit caps you see are now read directly from the on-chain cap registry, so the number always matches what the contract actually enforces.

entries.title: Revenue is now shown per network
entries.body: Our revenue view now covers every network we support — Base and Robinhood testnet — each shown separately so figures are never mixed across chains (they're in different tokens). We also stood up our fee-treasury multisig on Robinhood testnet at the exact same address as on Base, and pointed the Robinhood swap fee to it — so on every network the fees flow to the same 2-of-3 Safe that only receives and has no power over your funds.

entries.title: Protocol fees now flow to a multisig — with provably no power over you
entries.body: The fees SparkPoint earns now go to a dedicated 2-of-3 multisig treasury instead of a single wallet. Crucially, that treasury only receives fees — it can't pause or move the vault, isn't the guardian, and has no way to touch your deposits. You don't have to take our word for it: the Trust Center now reads the fee recipient live from the contract and shows its authority over your funds as none. Your withdraw-anytime right is completely unaffected.

entries.title: Revenue is now real, per stream
entries.body: Our internal revenue view is no longer a sample — it now reads live, on-chain figures for each way SparkPoint earns: the 0.20% swap routing fee, the 10% vault performance fee (only ever on gains, never your principal), and SRK membership. Each stream is honest about itself: if a source isn't wired up yet we show nothing rather than a made-up number, and a genuine zero shows as zero. We also show the fee treasury multisig's live balances with a plain statement of what it can and can't do — it only receives fees and has no power over your funds.

entries.title: Buy Premium with SRK
entries.body: You can now upgrade to Premium right in the app, paid in SRK. The Premium page shows your real SRK balance and the monthly price, and when you upgrade you sign the payment yourself — it goes straight to our disclosed treasury address, and we never move your funds for you. Once the payment confirms on-chain, Premium switches on automatically and shows when it renews. As always this is completely optional: the assistant, the vault, deposits, yield, swaps, and withdraw-anytime stay free and are never gated by Premium.

entries.title: Choose your vault
entries.body: You can now pick which vault to use on the Vault page — starting with our conservative launch vault plus a hand-picked option that routes to Morpho. Your choice carries through to deposit and withdraw. Two things never change: before any deposit, the app checks the vault is one we've verified (you'll see a ✓), and you can always withdraw your funds yourself, no matter what. Where a vault's yield rate isn't measured yet, we show a dash rather than a made-up number. (The second option is currently a testnet demo vault.)

entries.title: Fair limits for the AI assistant
entries.body: The AI assistant now has fair daily limits, so it stays fast and available for everyone. The free tier is generous and fully capable — your vault, deposits, swaps, and withdraw-anytime are never affected by a limit. If you reach the day's free limit, the assistant simply tells you, and it resets the next day. You can see how much you've used on the Premium page; Premium members get higher limits, priority when things are busy, and a smarter, faster AI model.

entries.title: Real token and network icons
entries.body: The Swap page and the network switcher now show real token logos (ETH, USDC, and more) and network logos, instead of just a symbol and a colored dot. A token without a known logo — like a brand-new or testnet token — falls back to a clean lettered badge. The icon is only for recognition: whether a token is verified is still shown separately, so a look-alike logo can never vouch for a token.

entries.title: Swap into any token — not just ETH and USDC
entries.body: The Swap page now works like a full DEX. Keep ETH and USDC as one-tap picks, or paste any token's contract address to swap into it. SparkPoint reads the token straight from the chain, finds the best route automatically — routing through WETH or USDC when there's no direct pool — and always shows whether a token is verified, asking you to confirm before you receive an unverified one. You still sign every swap from your own wallet; SparkPoint never holds your funds.

entries.title: Switching wallets is recognized right away
entries.body: If you switch to a different wallet in your browser extension — anywhere in the app — SparkPoint now picks up the new wallet immediately and asks you to sign in for it, instead of getting stuck on the previous wallet's access status. Your funds are never affected; withdrawals and exit stay open no matter what.

entries.title: SparkPoint keeps itself up to date
entries.body: When we ship an update, SparkPoint now quietly refreshes to the newest version and shows you what changed — including a quick welcome the first time you drop in — and it always waits until any transaction or unsaved work is safely finished first.

entries.title: Wallet holdings on every network
entries.body: Your Portfolio now lists your native ETH plus every token your wallet holds — on Base, Base Sepolia, and Robinhood testnet.

entries.title: Sparky has a consistent voice
entries.body: The assistant now speaks with one on-brand character — clearer and steadier, and still no hype or emoji.

entries.title: A live What's New feed
entries.body: Open the changelog any time from the left rail to see everything we've shipped to the alpha.

entries.title: Steadier chat
entries.body: Chat now recovers from brief gateway hiccups instead of failing a turn — fewer "hit a problem" messages.
